In fact, the response field in kibana_sample_data_logs is a text field with a .keyword subfield. A range query on a text field works if the values are numeric strings (ES parses them as numbers for range comparisons… actually, range queries on text fields work when all values are numeric, and they are compared as numbers).

Alternatively, I can use a query on response.keyword. The ES query JSON is a string:

Hmm, but range on .keyword works fine (keyword supports range queries when the values are sortable strings, and numeric strings sort numerically when the lengths are equal — all are 3 characters so that works, but it's safer to use the text field where ES coerces to numbers).

Actually, the safest bet is: `{"range":{"response":{"gte":500,"lte":599}}}`. Range queries on a text field: ES applies the numeric comparison when the values are numeric. In the kibana sample data, response values are "200", "301", "404", "500", etc. — all numeric, so this works.

```json
  "esQuery": "{\"query\":{\"range\":{\"response\":{\"gte\":500,\"lte\":599}}}}",
  "index": ["kibana_sample_data_logs"],
  "timeField": "timestamp",
  "threshold": [10],
  "thresholdComparator": ">",
  "timeWindowSize": 5,
  "timeWindowUnit": "m",
  "size": 100
}
```

thresholdComparator is ">", threshold is [10] — fires when the count exceeds 10. This matches "fire if 10 or more server errors arrive within 5 minutes."
